title: The four-day week
instructions: For questions 1-8, read the text below and decide which answer (A, B, C or D) best fits each gap.
text:
When a handful of companies first experimented with a four-day working week, sceptics [[1]] the idea as a passing fad. A decade later, the concept has gained considerable [[2]], with pilot schemes running in several European countries. The premise is simple: staff work fewer hours for the same pay, on the [[3]] that they will be more focused and therefore just as productive.

Early results have been encouraging, [[4]] not entirely conclusive. Participating firms report lower staff turnover and fewer days lost to illness, and many employees claim they would be reluctant to return to a conventional timetable. However, critics point out that the companies taking part were self-selected, a factor that may [[5]] the findings, since only those confident of a positive outcome were likely to sign up in the first place.

There are also sectors where the model is difficult to [[6]] into practice. Hospitals, emergency services and manufacturing plants that operate around the clock cannot simply close on Fridays; for them, a shorter week means recruiting additional staff, which [[7]] up costs considerably. Supporters concede this point but insist that the underlying principle, namely that output rather than hours spent at a desk should be the [[8]] of performance, remains sound.

questions.explanation: La estructura es «dismiss something as + sustantivo/adjetivo» (descartar algo por considerarlo...). «Ignore», «deny» y «refuse» no admiten «as» con este sentido.

«Gain momentum» es la colocación fija para «cobrar impulso/fuerza». «Impulse» en inglés es un impulso repentino o un arrebato, no progreso sostenido; «velocity» y «motion» son términos físicos que no colocan aquí.
«On the assumption that» (partiendo de la premisa de que) es una expresión fija. No existe «on the view/opinion/thought that».

«Adjetivo, if not + adjetivo» equivale a «aunque no del todo»: «encouraging, if not entirely conclusive». «Unless» es condicional, «whether» introduce alternativas y «despite» exige sustantivo o -ing.
«Skew the findings/results» significa sesgar o distorsionar los resultados. «Bend» se usa con «the rules» o «the truth»; «lean» es intransitivo y «tip» se usa con «the balance».
«Put something into practice» (llevar a la práctica) es la expresión fija. «Carry out» o «bring about» existen, pero no con «into practice».
«Drive up costs/prices» = hacer subir los costes. «Raise» es correcto sin «up» («raises costs»), pero «raises up costs» no es idiomático; «pull up» y «lift up» tienen sentido físico.
«The measure of performance» = el criterio con el que se mide el rendimiento. «Weight» es peso/importancia, «scale» es una escala graduada y «degree» indica grado o intensidad, no un criterio.

title: Locking out danger
instructions: For questions 1-8, read the text below and decide which answer (A, B, C or D) best fits each gap.
text:
In industrial maintenance, few procedures are as critical as lockout/tagout, which [[1]] the backbone of most safety management systems. The principle is straightforward: before anyone works on a machine, every source of hazardous energy must be isolated and the isolation point secured so that the equipment cannot be switched on [[2]] accident. Yet investigations into serious injuries repeatedly reveal that the procedure was either skipped or carried out in a perfunctory manner.

Part of the problem is cultural. When production targets are tight, there is strong pressure to [[3]] corners, and a technician who insists on following every step may be seen as obstructive. Supervisors therefore play a [[4]] role: if they tolerate shortcuts even once, they implicitly signal that safety rules are negotiable.

Another difficulty lies in stored energy. Isolating the electrical supply is not enough if a hydraulic line remains [[5]] pressure or a raised component could fall under its own weight. A thorough procedure must therefore include verification that all residual energy has been dissipated before work [[6]].

Leading companies have begun to [[7]] these weaknesses by digitising work permits and requiring each worker to attach a personal padlock to the isolation point. Only when the last lock has been removed can the machine be restarted. Such measures may seem cumbersome, but they are a small price to pay [[8]] avoiding life-changing injuries.

questions.explanation: «Form the backbone of» (constituir la columna vertebral de) es la colocación habitual. «Make», «construct» y «shape» no colocan con «backbone» en este sentido.
«By accident» = accidentalmente. «On accident» es coloquial y no estándar; «in» y «with» no forman la expresión.
«Cut corners» = hacer las cosas de forma chapucera para ahorrar tiempo o dinero. Es una expresión fija; los demás verbos no la forman.
«Play a pivotal role» = desempeñar un papel decisivo. «Hinging», «tipping» y «balancing» no funcionan como adjetivos con «role» («tipping point» sí existe, pero no aquí).
«Under pressure» es la preposición fija tanto en sentido físico (presión hidráulica) como figurado. «At pressure» solo aparece con un valor numérico («at 200 bar»).
«Work commences» (formal de «begins») es intransitivo, como exige la frase. «Initiate» y «launch» suelen ser transitivos (necesitan objeto) y «work opens» no tiene sentido.
«Address weaknesses/problems» = abordarlos, con objeto directo. «Attend», «cope» y «deal» necesitarían preposición («attend to», «cope with», «deal with»).
«A small price to pay for (doing) something» es una expresión fija: un sacrificio pequeño a cambio de algo valioso.

title: Policing by consent
instructions: For questions 1-8, read the text below and decide which answer (A, B, C or D) best fits each gap.
text:
Community policing rests on a deceptively simple idea: officers who know the neighbourhoods they patrol are better [[1]] to prevent crime than those who merely respond to emergency calls. By building relationships with residents, shopkeepers and local associations, they gain access to information that would otherwise never [[2]] to light.

Critics, however, argue that the approach is difficult to evaluate. Crimes that are prevented leave no trace in the statistics, so the benefits are easily [[3]] by the more visible demands of emergency response. When budgets are squeezed, neighbourhood teams are often the first to be cut, [[4]] the fact that rebuilding trust can take years.

Trust is, indeed, the [[5]] of the matter. In areas where relations with the police have historically been strained, residents may be reluctant to come [[6]] as witnesses, fearing reprisals or simply doubting that anything will be done. Officers who attend community meetings regularly and follow up on complaints can gradually [[7]] this scepticism, demonstrating through their actions that local concerns are taken seriously.

Ultimately, the success of community policing [[8]] on whether officers are genuinely willing to listen, rather than on the sheer number deployed. A patrol that stops to talk to a shopkeeper may achieve more in an afternoon than a dozen arrests.

questions.explanation: «Be better placed to do something» = estar en mejor posición para hacerlo. «Set to» significa «a punto de»; «put» y «laid» no forman esta expresión.
«Come to light» = salir a la luz (sin objeto). «Bring something to light» necesitaría objeto; «get» y «arrive» no forman la expresión.
«Be overshadowed by» = quedar eclipsado por algo más visible. «Overcast» se dice del cielo nublado, «overrun» de un lugar invadido y «overdrawn» de una cuenta en números rojos.
Solo «despite» puede ir seguido de «the fact that» + oración. «Although» introduce directamente una oración (sin «the fact that») y «however»/«nevertheless» son adverbios que no subordinan.
«The heart of the matter» = el meollo de la cuestión. Es una expresión fija; «centre», «middle» o «base» no la forman.
«Come forward (as a witness)» = presentarse voluntariamente para aportar información a la policía. «Come out» significa salir o hacerse público, y «come up/over» tienen otros sentidos.
«Dispel scepticism/doubts/fears» = disipar dudas o recelos. «Disperse» se usa con multitudes o gases, «dispense» significa repartir o prescindir («dispense with») y «displace» es desplazar.
«Hinge on» = depender por completo de. «Lean on» es apoyarse o presionar; «base» y «ground» son transitivos y requieren pasiva («is based on»).

meta.topic: Mine closure and acid mine drainage

title: Life after the mine
instructions: For questions 1-8, read the text below and decide which answer (A, B, C or D) best fits each gap.
text:
For much of the twentieth century, mining companies treated the land they excavated as a resource to be exploited and then abandoned. Today, by [[1]], a closure plan must be approved before extraction can even begin, and operators are required to set [[2]] funds to cover the full cost of rehabilitation.

One of the most persistent problems is acid mine drainage. When sulphide minerals exposed by excavation come into [[3]] with air and water, they produce sulphuric acid, which in turn leaches heavy metals from the surrounding rock. The resulting effluent can [[4]] rivers for decades, long after the mine itself has ceased operating.

Engineers have developed a range of techniques to get to [[5]] with the problem. Covering waste rock with impermeable layers limits the ingress of oxygen; adding crushed limestone raises the pH of the water; and passive treatment systems, such as constructed wetlands, rely on natural processes to remove metals. [[6]] of these methods is a panacea, however: each must be tailored to the geology and climate of the site.

Rehabilitation also has a social dimension. Communities that have lived alongside a mine for generations often hold firm views about what the land should be used for once operations [[7]] to an end. Involving them early in the planning process not only reduces the risk of conflict but also [[8]] the chances that the restored landscape will be valued and maintained.

questions.explanation: «By contrast» es el conector fijo para marcar oposición entre dos situaciones (antes/hoy). «By distinction», «by opposite» y «by reverse» no existen («in reverse» sí, pero con otro sentido).
«Set aside (funds)» = reservar dinero para un fin concreto. «Set apart» significa distinguir; «set off» es ponerse en marcha o provocar, y «set away» no existe.
«Come into contact with» = entrar en contacto con. «Get in touch» existe pero con otro verbo y sentido (comunicarse); «connection» y «reach» no forman la expresión.
«Contaminate rivers» = contaminar con sustancias nocivas. «Infest» se usa con plagas, «infect» con enfermedades y «intoxicate» significa embriagar (falso amigo de «intoxicar»).
«Get to grips with» = abordar con decisión un problema. «Come to terms with» existe, pero con «come» y significa aceptar; «get to hold/hands» no existen.
Se mencionan tres métodos, así que se usa «None of» (ninguno de más de dos). «Neither of» solo vale para dos elementos, «No» no va seguido de «of» y «Nothing of» no es idiomático.
«Come to an end» = llegar a su fin (intransitivo). «Bring something to an end» necesita objeto; «reach an end» no lleva «to» y «arrive to an end» no existe.
«Boost the chances» = aumentar las probabilidades. «Rise» es intransitivo (no lleva objeto); «grow» y «expand» no colocan con «chances».
